_note: ADDITIVE. contract/contract.json is under blind test and was NOT modified. H3 (worker to broker report) and H4 (broker to dispatcher delivery). Merge when the blind arm reports.
_report_provenance: The report field set is the one from the OLD NEXUS codebase, which survived 7 tasks across 3 workers on 2026-08-27 without amendment. nxb-004 recommended reusing the contract rather than the pipeline; this is that recommendation being taken.

worker_report.doc: What the WORKER produces. Handed to Codex as --output-schema so the runtime constrains it, rather than the broker parsing prose.

was_refused.doc: The worker's OWN claim that something was blocked. [M: nxb-002] a sandbox denial is invisible in the event stream, so this is the only channel that can carry it, and it is a claim not a measurement.

h3_receipt.doc: Emitted by the broker on observing a worker's report, before validating it.

outcome.doc: What H4 delivers. Two layers, kept separate on purpose: `delivery` is the broker's machinery, `report` is the WORKER'S CLAIM. Conflating them is how a clean pipeline gets read as a clean result.

provenance.doc: Includes refusal_scope: WHICH KINDS of refusal the RUNTIME can structurally report, drawn from a closed vocabulary, empty if none. A property of the runtime, recorded once, never mixed into the per-outcome effect field and never refused on. It replaced a boolean, which answered 'can this runtime report a refusal' with a yes that covered its permission layer and not the sandbox case the question was written for [nxb-029/033].

effect.doc: Whether this outcome's intended effect was checked from OUTSIDE the worker. UNCHECKED is the honest default and is NOT a failure: most work has no externally checkable effect. FALSIFIED means checked and found not to have happened.

h4_return.doc: What a dispatcher's collect call returns. R-050 amended: the call returns THE THING, never an acknowledgement that a thing was sent.

items.rule: H4 never blocks. You cannot block on a peer that is busy doing the work you gave it.
Non-delivery is surfaced by a QUERYABLE LIST that never clears itself, not by a timed alarm. A timer needs a budget and no budget has been measured.
An outcome is DELIVERED only when the dispatcher collects it. A push whose return value is a transmission ack proves nothing. [M: nxb-006]
Broker delivery state and worker-reported status are never merged into one field.

Ratification MUST refuse on FALSIFIED and MUST NOT refuse on UNCHECKED. A refusal that fires on every outcome a runtime can produce teaches nothing and is switched off; the same asymmetry that fail-open-on-unproven applies here.

WHICH KINDS of refusal a runtime can report is recorded in provenance as a property of the runtime, never as a property of an individual outcome, and never as a single boolean: a runtime can report one kind and not another, and a flag cannot say so.

_vocabulary_note: H3 HAD NO PUBLISHED VOCABULARY AT ALL while emitting five reasons, which is the largest single instance of the drift contract.json's _vocabulary_rule now forbids. `no_output_file` and `turn_failed` are the broker's own observations; the two `runtime_announced_*` terms are the runtime's own failure announcement, consumed rather than inferred, which turns a whole-budget wait into a sub-second refusal [nxb-025, measured nxb-022]. [nxb-042]

refusal_scope_vocabulary._doc: WHAT KINDS of refusal a runtime can structurally REPORT. A property of the runtime, recorded once in provenance and NEVER refused on. Published here in nxb-042: it was born in code as a closed dict, which contract.json's _vocabulary_rule forbids, and a closed vocabulary no contract publishes is a capability claim living in a file. Separate from refusal_vocabulary because these are not reasons a dispatch is refused; they describe a RUNTIME.
refusal_scope_vocabulary.harness_mediated: The runtime's own permission layer refused a tool call and emitted a structural event identifying it AS a refusal, independent of what the model then narrated. Measured present on Claude Code, absent on Codex.
refusal_scope_vocabulary.sandbox: An OS or sandbox refusal of an effect INSIDE a tool the runtime already permitted is reported as a refusal. MEASURED ABSENT ON BOTH RUNTIMES: published as an honest negative, so a consumer can tell 'no runtime covers this' from 'nobody looked'.
refusal_scope_vocabulary._removed: `opaque_tool_failure` was a third token and was removed in nxb-034. It answered a different question: the other two say a refusal IS REPORTED, it said a FAILURE IS VISIBLE without being named a refusal. A negative in a list of positives made the list non-monotonic and broke the emptiness test this vocabulary's own reader blesses. The FACT it carried is real and measured and currently has no home; see FAILURE-VISIBILITY-HOMELESS, deliberately still unpublished.
